ROLE: Append len raw bytes (which may contain NUL and any binary value) to the buffer with all-or-nothing failure semantics.

SIGNATURE.RAW: int buffer_append(struct byte_buf *buf, const void *src, size_t len)
SIGNATURE.NAME: buffer_append

FUNC.NAME: buffer_reserve
FUNC.ROLE: Guarantee capacity for the whole append in one step

CALL_CONTRACTS.NAME: buffer_reserve
CALL_CONTRACTS.RETURN: 0 when cap >= len + extra; -1 on overflow or allocation failure
CALL_CONTRACTS.OWNERSHIP: no ownership transfer; the buffer keeps its storage or grows it
CALL_CONTRACTS.FAILURE: -1 leaves the buffer contents and capacity unchanged, so the caller must not write anything and must return failure

LOGIC.INPUT: buf (NULL allowed), src pointing to len caller-owned bytes (may be NULL only when len is 0), len.
LOGIC.ACTION: 1) If buf is NULL return -1. 2) If len == 0 return 0 without reading src (an empty append is a successful no-op, which is what preserves an empty PUBLISH payload). 3) If src is NULL return -1. 4) If buffer_reserve(buf, len) != 0 return -1: nothing was written and no byte of the previous contents changed. 5) memcpy(buf->data + buf->len, src, len) then buf->len += len; return 0. src is borrowed and never retained, so a caller may pass a slice of a packet buffer and may free it immediately after the call.
LOGIC.OUTPUT: 0 when all len bytes are appended in order and len grew by exactly len; -1 when no byte was appended and the previous contents are untouched.
INVARIANTS_USED: no implicit NUL terminator is added
binary payload bytes including 0x00 are stored verbatim
LOGIC.PRECONDITION: buf is NULL or a valid buffer; src points to at least len readable bytes when len > 0.
LOGIC.POSTCONDITION: On success the last len bytes of the buffer equal src[0..len-1] and len increased by len; on failure the buffer is unchanged.
LOGIC.THREAD_SAFETY: Not thread safe; the caller owns the buffer exclusively.
